attachToSpec.description: Deterministic kinematic follow: reuses scene.assets[].anchor's own vocabulary (position/followAssetId + % offsets + edge), resolved fresh every frame against the followed asset's LIVE box (its baked resolvedPhysics position when it's itself a dynamic body, or its static resolvedPosition otherwise) instead of once at scene start.

followAssetId.description: Asset id (this scene) whose live per-frame box this asset rides along with. May be a Matter-simulated dynamic body, a static anchor, or a plain non-physics asset (e.g. a moving motion.js asset) — any asset with a resolvedPosition/resolvedPhysics track.

anchorEdge.description: Which point on the FOLLOWED asset's box to ride. Same vocabulary as scene.assets[].anchor.anchorEdge.

landAtSpec.description: Deterministic parabolic toss: computes the exact initial velocity needed (closed-form, given scenePhysicsSpec.gravity) so this body's Matter-simulated trajectory reaches the target position at EXACTLY atFrame — no more hand-tuning initialVelocity/angle to eyeball a landing spot. The body is still stepped through Matter each frame (so it can still collide/bounce with OTHER bodies en route), but its launch velocity is solved rather than authored.

atFrame.description: Scene-local frame the body must reach the target position at. Must be > startFrame.

targetAssetId.description: Asset id (this scene) whose anchor-resolved center is the landing point, read once at resolve time (not live-tracked — for a live-tracked ride, use attachTo on the ARRIVING asset instead, or land at this asset then attachTo it afterward). Mutually exclusive with target.

target.description: Absolute composition-space landing point in px. Mutually exclusive with targetAssetId.

gravity.description: Default { x: 0, y: 1 } — Matter's own 'earth gravity' unit (scaled internally by engine.gravity.scale, default 0.001), tuned for pixel-space worlds out of the box.

gravityScale.description: Override for engine.gravity.scale. Leave unset to use Matter's default (0.001).

iterations.description: Matter constraint/position/velocity solver iterations. Default: Matter's own default (6).

startFrame.description: Scene-local frame the simulation begins stepping at. Every frame before this holds all dynamic bodies at their initial resolved position (pre-drop).

constraints.description: Point-to-point joints (Matter.Constraint) linking two physics bodies, or one body to a fixed world point — the primitive a free-body/force/magnet vocabulary alone can't express: a rigid pivot a beam swings around (a balance scale's fulcrum, a see-saw, a pendulum), as opposed to a body merely accelerating toward a target. Resolved AFTER every scene.assets[].physics body exists but BEFORE the simulation steps, so both endpoints must reference asset ids that carry a physics block in THIS scene.

id.description: Optional label, for error messages only — not referenced elsewhere.

bodyA.description: Asset id (this scene) of the first body the joint attaches to. Must carry a physics block.

pointA.description: Attachment point on bodyA, as a LOCAL offset in px from bodyA's own center (NOT world-space, NOT a percent — Matter's own convention). Default { x: 0, y: 0 } — the body's center, e.g. a beam pinned at its own midpoint.

bodyB.description: Asset id (this scene) of the second body the joint attaches to. Omit to anchor bodyA to a FIXED WORLD POINT instead (see pointB) — the common 'pin this beam to an immovable fulcrum' shape, cheaper than authoring a second static body when the anchor point doesn't need its own rendered asset.

pointB.description: When bodyB is set: a LOCAL offset in px from bodyB's own center, same convention as pointA. When bodyB is omitted: an absolute WORLD-SPACE point (composition px) the joint anchors bodyA's pointA to — resolve this against the composition's own coordinate space, not a percent. Default { x: 0, y: 0 }.

length.description: Rest distance the joint tries to maintain between pointA and pointB, in px. 0 (default) pins the two points together — a rigid hinge/pivot (the point stays fixed, but the body remains free to ROTATE about it, since a single point constraint doesn't resist rotation). A nonzero length behaves like a rigid rod holding the two points that far apart — e.g. a swinging pendulum arm.

stiffness.description: 1 (default) = rigid, effectively unstretchable — the correct value for a pivot/hinge. Lower values behave like a soft spring instead (bouncier, stretches under load) — rarely what a 'pivot' interaction wants, but available for a springy-tether look.

damping.description: Resists relative velocity along the constraint (reduces oscillation). 0 = undamped. Only meaningful when stiffness < 1 — a rigid (stiffness:1) pin has no oscillation to damp.

followPathSpec.description: Deterministic 'plot points, smooth curve, follow it' primitive: an authored sequence of 3+ points becomes a Catmull-Rom spline (same math WavyLine/resolveWavyPath uses) and the asset travels along that curve's actual arc length, reaching the LAST point at exactly atFrame — no velocity/gravity involved, just a point-in-time-along-the-curve lookup. Like landAt/attachTo, this excludes the asset from the Matter world entirely.

points.description: Waypoints in scene-assets authoring order (NOT resolved-pixel order — each item uses the shared named-corner/followAssetId/raw-{x,y} vocabulary, shared.schema.json#/definitions/anchorPointSpec). 2 points is a straight/wavy line (same as WavyLine's 2-point case); 3+ points is smoothed into one continuous Catmull-Rom curve — no hand-authored bezier control points needed.

atFrame.description: Scene-local frame the asset reaches the FINAL point. Must be greater than scene.physics.startFrame. Travel is paced by real arc length along the curve (not by point index), so unevenly-spaced waypoints don't cause uneven speed.

curveAmount.description: Same bow/offset knob as WavyLine's styleOverride.curveAmount — only meaningful with exactly 2 points (ignored once smoothCurve's 3+-point spline kicks in, matching buildWavyPathD's own precedence).

rotateToPath.description: When true, the asset's rotateDeg each frame follows the curve's own tangent angle (nose pointed the direction of travel) instead of staying at 0 — e.g. an arrow or vehicle following a route.

startFrame.description: Scene-local frame the asset LEAVES the first point (travel begins). Default 0 — travel spans the asset's full [0, atFrame] window. Distinct from scene.physics.startFrame (which only gates the Matter simulation) — this asset isn't simulated at all.

bodyType.description: 'dynamic': simulated — falls/bounces under gravity and collisions, and gets a baked resolvedPhysics.frames[] track. 'static': an immovable anchor other bodies can collide with (a ledge, floor, wall); never moves regardless of gravity, and gets NO resolvedPhysics track — it renders at its normal resolvedPosition, unchanged. Note: shape: 'path' requires bodyType: 'static'. Ignored (but still required) when attachTo, landAt, or followPath is set — those fields opt this asset OUT of the Matter simulation entirely in favor of a deterministic kinematic track; author bodyType: 'dynamic' by convention in that case.

attachTo.description: Deterministic 'ride along' primitive: this asset's position is recomputed every frame from another asset's LIVE box (simulated or static) via the same anchor vocabulary scene.assets[].anchor uses, instead of being simulated by Matter. Mutually exclusive in effect with landAt (author at most one); when set, this asset is excluded from the Matter world entirely — no mass/friction/collision — so it cannot itself be the target of another body's magnet/force/collidesWith, and it cannot follow another attachTo/landAt asset (no chaining).

landAt.description: Deterministic 'cartoon toss' primitive: a closed-form parabolic arc from this asset's anchor-resolved start position to an exact target point/asset, guaranteed to land exactly on time — no velocity/gravity tuning needed. Like attachTo, this excludes the asset from the Matter world (no collisions/bounce once landAt is used) and cannot target another attachTo/landAt asset.

followPath.description: Deterministic 'plot points, smooth curve, follow it' primitive: author 2+ waypoints, get a Catmull-Rom spline, the asset travels it and reaches the final point at exactly atFrame. Mutually exclusive with attachTo/landAt (author at most one); excludes the asset from the Matter world entirely, same as attachTo/landAt.

pathSegments.description: Only used with shape:'path'. Number of straight sub-segments the resolved curve (asset.content._path, e.g. a WavyLine) is chopped into to approximate a collision surface — Matter has no native bezier body. Higher = smoother collisions, more bodies.

radius.description: Circle radius in px. Only used when shape is 'circle'; defaults to min(width,height)/2.

frictionAir.description: Air resistance. 0 lets a dynamic body fall/slide forever without damping.

initialVelocity.description: px/frame at simulation start. Default { x: 0, y: 0 }.

fixedRotation.description: Body never rotates (infinite inertia) — e.g. a card that should slide/bounce but stay upright.

collidesWith.description: Asset ids (same scene) this body may collide with. Omit to collide with every other physics body in the scene (default).

vector.description: Raw acceleration in px/frame² — the SAME units as initialVelocity, deliberately NOT Matter's mass-scaled applyForce() API, so this stays predictable and composes cleanly with gravity/initialVelocity instead of needing a separate mental model. Prefer towardAssetId/magnitude when the push direction is meant to track another asset instead of a fixed compass heading.

towardAssetId.description: Another asset id in this scene that ALSO carries a `physics` block (dynamic or static). Direction is recomputed every simulated step toward that target's LIVE centroid position, same targeting model as physics.magnet.targetAssetId — use this instead of `vector` so the push stays relative to a body rather than a fixed absolute heading.

magnitude.description: Acceleration in px/frame², applied along the live direction toward towardAssetId. Only used with towardAssetId; ignored/invalid alongside vector.

oneShot.description: true: applied once, as an instantaneous velocity kick, at startFrame — a shove. false (default): applied every simulated frame within [startFrame, endFrame) — a sustained push, e.g. wind.

endFrame.description: Scene-local frame the continuous force stops (exclusive). Omit to apply for the rest of the simulation. Ignored when oneShot is true.

targetAssetId.description: Another asset id in this scene that ALSO carries a `physics` block (dynamic or static — a static anchor is the common case, e.g. an invisible marker placed where you want the body to climb toward). This body accelerates toward that target's live simulated position every step.

strength.description: Attraction acceleration, px/frame². This is the energy source that can make a body climb — gravity+friction alone never will.

falloff.description: 'none': constant pull regardless of distance (predictable, recommended for a deliberate 'climb to this point' effect). 'linear'/'quadratic': weaker the farther away.

maxDistance.description: Only pulls within this px distance of the target. Omit for unlimited range.

endFrame.description: Scene-local frame the pull stops (exclusive). Omit to pull for the rest of the simulation.

attractTo.description: 'centroid' (default, unchanged): pull toward the target body's center of mass. 'nearestSurfacePoint': pull toward the closest point on the target's boundary — for a rectangle/circle this is the nearest edge point; for a shape:'path' target (e.g. a WavyLine used as a magnet anchor), this is the nearest point on the actual curve, sampled from content._path, not the compound body's misleading centroid.

sceneId.description: An EARLIER scene (in manifest.scenes order) whose matching physics asset's FINAL baked frame — position, angle, and finite-differenced velocity — seeds this asset's initial simulation state, instead of starting from anchor/initialVelocity at rest. This is a resolve-time simulation-state carry, distinct from transitionOut.params.carryAssetId (which only passes resolvedPosition/resolvedStyle to the transition component for a visual crossfade during the cut, and never touches physics).

assetId.description: Asset id within sceneId to carry from. Defaults to this asset's own id — the common case: same logical coin, same id, in both scenes.
